text:
Alex Tuch scored twice and added an assist, and in a game that finished 5-4 for Washington, that was enough to split a contest the numbers say was nearly dead even. The Capitals deserved to win 52 percent of the time, a margin barely bigger than a coin flip, and at even strength the chances were almost identical (2.38 expected goals for Washington, 2.22 for Montreal). The first two periods belonged to the visitors in the second, when Montreal out-created Washington 1.59 to 0.88, and the first was a draw. Josh Anderson scored twice for the Canadiens, and his second, a 28 percent chance, tied it 3-3 in the second.

The third period decided it. Washington generated 2.70 expected goals to Montreal's 0.68, and the goals arrived in a hurry. Justin Holl's snap shot at 12:29 had a 2 percent chance of going in, a low-percentage look that beat Jakub Dobes and put Washington ahead 4-3. Tuch followed at 17:05 for a 5-3 lead. Dobes finished 1.81 goals worse than expected, and Charlie Lindgren, at 0.94 below expected, was not much better, so neither goalie bailed out his team.

Tuch had already scored shorthanded in the second, a 4 percent slap shot that gave Washington a lead it hadn't earned by the run of play. Nick Suzuki cut it to 5-4 on the power play at 18:21, assisted by Lane Hutson, but Montreal ran out of time despite 68 shot attempts to Washington's 52. The Canadiens did the volume work. The Capitals took the one period that mattered and a couple of improbable goals, which is how a near-even game ended with a one-goal result.
